Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 09:30 AM PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Amy Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jenna Wright (Redwood CSM); Priya Kumar (Beacon CTO), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Liam O'Neill (Infra), Nora Diaz (Product)

Summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark runs comparing Redwood inference against baseline provider (ProviderX). Covered latency (p50/p95), sustained throughput, tuning knobs (batch size, KV cache, quantization), and infra differences. Agreed to run extended throughput test on customer's environment and share raw logs; customer to provide production traffic profile. Security docs next.

Topics: latency numbers, throughput scaling, KV cache effectiveness, quantization tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted, next-step benchmark runs, security follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Amy Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, we have the usual folks from beacon?
[00:10] Priya Kumar: yep, priya here, samir, liam, nora also on.
[00:15] Diego Ramos: hi all, diego here, i'll walk through the benchmark slides and the raw numbers we ran last week.
[00:20] Samir Patel: great, excited — been looking forward to numbers.

[01:02] Diego Ramos: ok so high level — we did three classes of tests: single-request latency (p50/p95), sustained throughput (closed-loop qps), and an end-to-end app ish test with a prefix cache enabled. note: baseline provider is ProviderX runs we pulled from your earlier spreadsheet and our lab runs, so not 1:1 but comparable.
[01:22] Priya Kumar: fair, thanks.

[02:10] Diego Ramos: numbers — for the 1k token-ish prompt (avg response ~400 tokens) on our quantized 4-bit profile, redwood p50 was about 120 ms, p95 ~420 ms. ProviderX p50 ~210 ms, p95 ~860 ms. so roughly 40-50% improvement on p50, and about 2x on p95 in our lab runs.
[02:40] Samir Patel: wait, 120 ms for p50 for a 400 token response? can you clarify units — is that per token or end-to-end?
[02:47] Diego Ramos: yeah good call, it's end-to-end wall clock per request from send to first token received in streaming mode, not per-token. transcription note, sometimes the auto transcription swapped tokens for tokes, etc.

[04:05] Priya Kumar: that's a pretty big delta on p95, what's driving the tail for providerX?
[04:12] Diego Ramos: two main things — their defaults had small batch sizes and no KV prefix caching. also in our runs they hit head-of-line blocking when requests spiked, whereas our continuous batching+adaptive kernel selection handled bursts better. we also made a tuning change: bumped batch size to 8 for this run — that reduced p50 without hurting p95 much.
[05:00] Liam O'Neill: curious on memory behavior — were these runs on the same GPU type? we run on A100 equivalent, ProviderX runs were on A100 as well?
[05:08] Diego Ramos: yes both A100 class; we annotated the spreadsheet with instance types. in the raw logs you'll see memory high-water marks; our quantized run used slightly less GPU memory which helped with concurrency.

[06:20] Samir Patel: throughput numbers? we need to see sustained qps since our traffic is bursty at 300 concurrency.
[06:27] Diego Ramos: sustained throughput — lab harness: Redwood 120 req/s sustained, ProviderX 75 req/s under same load generator and request profile. On the customer's smaller test bed we got 95 req/s due to network+env differences. With autotune and prefix cache on, effective tokens per request dropped ~28% in the app test, so token cost reduced proportionally.
[07:05] Priya Kumar: 120 req/s vs 75 is significant. what's the cost delta? per 1M tokens?
[07:12] Amy Chen: rough estimate from our model & quant profile — about 20-30% lower unit cost for Redwood when you account for reduced tokens (cache) and higher throughput. Diego will send the cost calc and assumptions.

[08:00] Samir Patel: the token reduction — how deterministic is it? our prompts vary a lot.
[08:06] Diego Ramos: it's workload dependent; for your FAQ-style traffic we saw higher prefix reuse so more benefit. for open-ended generation it's less. we'll include per-prompt breakdown in the spreadsheet.

[09:30] Nora Diaz: question on quality — did you run evals to compare generation quality vs ProviderX?
[09:37] Diego Ramos: yes we ran nll and a small human eval on a 200-sample subset — quality delta was negligible. note that quantization profile used preserves fp16-equivalent accuracy for common prompts; we flagged a few edge cases where you might prefer fp16 fallback.

[11:10] Priya Kumar: re: dedicated vs hosted — our security team favors VPC/private deployment for PHI reasons. any blockers?
[11:20] Amy Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC & on-prem options; we have KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. security team will want SOC2 + HIPAA docs. Jenna will coordinate.
[11:32] Jenna Wright: yes i'll follow up with SOC2 artifact pack and HIPAA addendum — expect that by end of week.

[13:00] Liam O'Neill: quick infra nit — for the long-run throughput test we want to run on our staging cluster (same IP routing, same NAT) to surface any network jitter. can you run the long 2-hour run in our env?
[13:10] Diego Ramos: absolutely — diego will run the extended run, we'll capture p50/p95, CUDA metrics, GPU utilization, and memory HF, plus any retransmits.
[13:20] Amy Chen: we'll need ssh creds or a restricted test harness; liam, please send access details.

[15:00] Samir Patel: about quantization — are you using Q4 or Q8? and if we need fp16 for edge prompts, how easy is fallback?
[15:08] Diego Ramos: Q4 profile for these runs with calibrated per-channel quantization. fallback is straightforward — it's an alternate model variant we can route to automatically when prompt matches a flagged pattern, but it costs more. we can show cost+latency tradeoffs.

[17:10] Priya Kumar: any concerns about model compatibility with our custom finetunes? we plan to deploy a tuned LLM for clinical triage.
[17:18] Diego Ramos: compatible — we can host the tuned weights, but we need to test KV cache behavior since fine-tuned tokenization differences can affect prefix matching. we'll add that to the run plan.

[19:00] Amy Chen: ok quick housekeeping — the spreadsheet in the share drive has three tabs: lab-runs, customer-mini, and cost-model. raw logs are in the bucket link we shared earlier (note: link in chat).

[21:30] Samir Patel: on the ProviderX runs, any chance they were using a different batching policy? wondering if we can replicate exactly to be apples-to-apples.
[21:38] Diego Ramos: we tried to match as best as possible, but vendor defaults differ; we reached out to ProviderX but didn't get full settings. that said, we replicated their config as documented in your earlier file and flagged assumptions in the spreadsheet.

[24:00] Priya Kumar: on tail latencies — you mentioned head-of-line blocking — can you explain briefly so our infra folks understand?
[24:07] Diego Ramos: sure — when batchers use fixed windows and a large request arrives it can block subsequent small low-latency requests from being served until that batch completes; our continuous batching pipeline prioritizes short requests and can cut batch windows adaptively to reduce tail. transcript note: sometimes speaker labels flip in auto export.

[26:50] Liam O'Neill: for the long-run run, can you also capture GPU clock throttling events and system temperature? in prior vendor runs we saw thermal throttling at 3+ hour marks.
[26:58] Diego Ramos: yes will include. we'll also include perf counters and kernel-level timings.

[29:10] Nora Diaz: product question — if we go dedicated, what's the rollout path? can we start hosted then fast migrate?
[29:16] Amy Chen: yes customers often start hosted for quick iteration and then move to Dedicated with a canary phase. Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts plus automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is saturated.

[31:00] Priya Kumar: timeline — we need to decide by end of month. is that realistic if Diego completes the long-run by 8/25 and we review by 8/27?
[31:08] Amy Chen: yes that fits. we'll aim for decision window end of August.

[33:00] Samir Patel: small note — there were a few transcription typos in previous files where KV cache became KV cash — ignore those.

[34:30] Diego Ramos: technical caveat — some edge-case prompts increased tokenization mismatch which reduced prefix cache hit rate; we'll include token-level diffs per prompt in the raw logs so you can see where hits dropped.

[36:00] Priya Kumar: ok final ask: please include p99 numbers too even if noisy.
[36:06] Diego Ramos: will do. the p99 in our lab runs was ~980 ms; ProviderX p99 was ~2.1s — we'll add caveats.

[38:10] Amy Chen: recap quick: diego runs extended throughput in your staging (liam provides access), amy shares spreadsheet + cost calc by 8/20, jenna shares SOC2/HIPAA artifacts by end of week, liam shares traffic profile by 8/21. decision window by end of August.
[38:35] Priya Kumar: yep that's good.
[38:40] Nora Diaz: thanks everyone.

[40:00] Amy Chen: any other blockers?
[40:05] Samir Patel: none from me.
[40:10] Liam O'Neill: none.
[41:00] Amy Chen: great, thanks for the time, we'll follow up in email with links and next steps.
[41:10] Diego Ramos: thanks all.
[41:20] Priya Kumar: bye.

Meeting end.
